title: Poison and Medicine Safety
hook: Most poisonings happen with a parent home but distracted. Store medicines and cleaners locked, up, and in their original containers — and save Poison Control: 1-800-222-1222.
key_points: Keep medicines, cleaners, and detergent packets locked, up high, out of sight — and always in their original containers.
Save the U.S. Poison Help line — 1-800-222-1222 — in your phone; it's free, expert, and confidential.
Watch for special dangers: button batteries can burn through tissue within hours, magnets, and liquid laundry detergent pods.
If you suspect poisoning, call Poison Control right away; don't make your child vomit — but call your local emergency number for trouble breathing or unresponsiveness.
content_html: A surprising fact reframes poison safety: most poisonings happen while a parent or caregiver is home but momentarily distracted. So the goal is to make the dangerous stuff genuinely hard to reach. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends storing medicines, cleaning products, and laundry detergent packets locked up, up high, out of sight — and always in their original containers, so nothing gets mistaken for food or drink. And before you ever need it, save the U.S. Poison Help line, 1-800-222-1222, in your phone; it's free, expert, and confidential.
extra_html: A few hazards deserve extra vigilance. Swallowed button batteries can cause serious tissue damage within a couple of hours, high-powered magnets can injure the gut, and liquid laundry detergent pods are concentrated and tempting to little hands. If you think your child has been poisoned and they're alert, call Poison Control right away — and don't try to make them vomit. If they're having trouble breathing, are very drowsy, or unresponsive, call your local emergency number immediately. This is general guidance — take a hands-on infant first-aid/CPR class, and in an emergency call your local emergency number.

flashcards.prompt: What's the U.S. Poison Help number, and what should you know about it?
flashcards.back_html: 1-800-222-1222 — free, expert, and confidential. Save it in your phone before you ever need it.

flashcards.prompt: If you suspect your child swallowed something poisonous and they're alert, what should you do?

choices.text: Call Poison Control right away and do not make them vomit
Make them vomit to get it out quickly
Wait and see if symptoms appear

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP says to contact Poison Control immediately and not to induce vomiting or use syrup of ipecac. Call your local emergency number for trouble breathing or unresponsiveness.

flashcards.prompt: Why are button batteries an especially urgent poisoning hazard?

choices.text: Swallowed, they can cause serious tissue damage within a couple of hours
They only matter if more than one is swallowed

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP notes serious tissue damage can occur in as little as two hours, so a swallowed button battery needs emergency care.
